# Overview

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/

moonpeak is one npm package with three jobs:

- **An MCP App framework.** One file per tool, one folder per View. React hooks for tool data, theme, display modes, state and host actions. The same project runs as a ChatGPT App, a Claude connector and in every other MCP Apps host.
- **An MCP testing framework.** Simulations, schema and View checks, Playwright e2e against ChatGPT and Claude style hosts, visual regression and real-model evals. It also tests MCP servers written in any language.
- **An MCP App inspector.** ChatGPT-style and Claude-style hosts on localhost, with every host setting in the URL.

```bash
npx moonpeak new
```

It is built on the official [MCP Apps SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) and the MCP TypeScript SDK v2, so what works in the inspector works in real hosts.

## Where to start

| If you want to | Read |
|---|---|
| Build your first app | [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) |
| Understand the folders | [Project scaffold](/docs/project-scaffold) |
| Write a tool or a View | [Tools](/docs/app-framework/tools) · [Views](/docs/app-framework/views) |
| Look up a hook | [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis) |
| Test an existing MCP server | [Any MCP server](/docs/testing/any-server) |
| Ship it | [Deployment](/docs/guides/deployment) |
| Learn the protocol | [MCP Apps introduction](/docs/mcp-apps) |

## Try the live demo

The starter app runs at `https://moonpeak-ai.com/mcp`. Add it as a custom connector in Claude, as an app in ChatGPT developer mode, or open it in the inspector:

```bash
npx moonpeak inspect --server https://moonpeak-ai.com/mcp
```

## For agents

Every docs page has a Markdown version (add `index.md` to its URL). [llms.txt](/docs/llms.txt) lists them all and [llms-full.txt](/docs/llms-full.txt) has every page in one file. The repository also ships an [agent skill](https://github.com/ghiansalman30-crypto/moonpeak/blob/main/skills/moonpeak/SKILL.md) for Claude Code and other coding agents.

# Quickstart

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/quickstart/

## 1. Create a project

```bash
npx moonpeak new
```

`new` asks three things:

1. **Project name**, for example `moon-app`.
2. **Resources**: which starter Views to include. Pick any of `moon`, `calendar` and `review`, or press Enter for all of them.
3. **Install dependencies?** Press Enter to install with the package manager you ran it with (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun).

You can skip the questions:

```bash
npx moonpeak new moon-app calendar,review --install
```

## 2. Start the inspector

```bash
cd moon-app
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000. The inspector lists your tools, runs the selected one and renders its View in a ChatGPT-style host. Switch to the Claude host, dark theme, a phone width or fullscreen from the sidebar. Your MCP server is live at http://localhost:3000/mcp.

## 3. Change something

Edit `src/resources/moon/moon.tsx` and save: the View updates in place and keeps its state. Edit `src/tools/show-moon.ts` and the next call uses the new code. No restart.

## 4. Test it

```bash
npm test                      # schemas, Views and simulations, in seconds
npx playwright install chromium
npx moonpeak test --e2e       # Playwright against the inspector
```

## 5. Run it in Claude or ChatGPT

```bash
npm run build && npm start    # http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

Put that behind HTTPS (see [Deployment](/docs/guides/deployment)), then:

- **Claude**: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → `https://your-domain/mcp`
- **ChatGPT**: Settings → Apps → enable Developer mode → Create app → `https://your-domain/mcp`

Ask *"what does the moon look like on Nov 24?"* and the moon View renders in the chat.

## Next

- [Project scaffold](/docs/project-scaffold): what every folder does
- [Tools](/docs/app-framework/tools) and [Views](/docs/app-framework/views)
- [Simulations](/docs/testing/simulations)

# Project scaffold

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/project-scaffold/

```
moon-app/
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  playwright.config.ts
  moonpeak.config.js        optional
  src/
    tools/                  one MCP tool per file
      show-moon.ts
      moon-facts.ts
    resources/              one View per folder
      moon/
        moon.tsx
        moon.css
    lib/                    shared code
  tests/
    simulations/            fixtures for the inspector and moonpeak test
      show-moon.json
    e2e/                    Playwright tests
      moon.spec.ts
    evals/                  model evals
      moon.eval.json
```

## Discovery rules

| Folder | Rule |
|---|---|
| `src/tools/*.ts` (also `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mts`, `.mjs`) | Every file is one tool. The file name is the tool name. `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and `*.d.ts` are ignored. |
| `src/resources/<name>/<name>.tsx` | Every folder is one View, served as `ui://<app>/<name>.html`. A `<name>.css`, `style.css` or `styles.css` next to it is included. |
| `tests/simulations/*.json` | One file per tool, holding one simulation or an array of them. |
| `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` | Run by `moonpeak test --e2e`. |
| `tests/evals/*.eval.json` | Run by `moonpeak test --eval`. |

The app name (used in resource URIs) is `name` from `moonpeak.config.js`, else `name` from `package.json`.

## Scripts

| Script | Runs |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | `moonpeak dev`: inspector + MCP server with hot reload |
| `npm test` | `moonpeak test` |
| `npm run test:e2e` | `moonpeak test --e2e` |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` |
| `npm run build` | `moonpeak build` |
| `npm start` | `moonpeak start` |

## Starter resources

`new` can include any of three example Views. Each comes with its tools, simulations, e2e tests and evals, so you can delete the ones you don't need without breaking the others.

- [moon](/docs/resources/moon): a detail card
- [calendar](/docs/resources/calendar): a carousel
- [review](/docs/resources/review): a review and confirm flow


---

# Configuration

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/configuration/

Create `moonpeak.config.js` (or `.mjs`) in the project root and export an object:

```js
// moonpeak.config.js
export default {
  name: "moon-app",              // app name in ui:// URIs; defaults to package.json name
  version: "1.2.0",              // server version; defaults to package.json version
  instructions: "Use show-moon for anything about the moon on a date.",
  port: 3000,                    // dev server port
  vite: {
    plugins: [],                 // extra Vite plugins for your Views (e.g. Tailwind)
    resolve: { alias: {} },
    define: {},
    css: {},
  },
};
```

| Key | Used by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | resource URIs, server info | `package.json` name, then the folder name |
| `version` | server info | `package.json` version, then `0.0.0` |
| `instructions` | MCP `initialize` instructions sent to the host | none |
| `port` | `moonpeak dev` | 3000, or the next free port |
| `vite` | building Views in dev and `moonpeak build` | moonpeak's own React setup |

## Tailwind or other Vite plugins

```js
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";
export default { vite: { plugins: [tailwindcss()] } };
```

Then `@import "tailwindcss";` in your View's CSS file.

## Per-View settings

Settings for one View live next to it, as `export const resource = {...}` in the View file. See [Views](/docs/app-framework/views#resource-config).


---

# Tools

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/tools/

```ts
// src/tools/show-moon.ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { moonOn, parseDate } from "../lib/moon";

export const tool = {
  title: "Show moon phase",
  description: "Show the moon phase for a date. Use when the user asks about the moon on a date.",
  resource: "moon",                     // render src/resources/moon as the UI
  annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },
  invoking: "Looking up",               // ChatGPT status while running
  invoked: "Here's the moon",           // ...and after
};

export const schema = {
  date: z.string().optional().describe("Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today."),
};

export default async function showMoon({ date }: { date?: string }) {
  return moonOn(parseDate(date));       // a plain object becomes structuredContent
}
```

## Exports

| Export | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | yes | The handler: `(input, ctx) => result`. May be async. |
| `tool` | yes | Metadata (below). |
| `schema` | no | Input schema: a zod raw shape (`{ date: z.string() }`) or a zod object (any Standard Schema). |
| `outputSchema` | no | Output schema, same forms. Hosts can validate `structuredContent` against it. |

## `tool` fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `description` | Written for the model: say what the tool does and when to use it. This is what evals test. |
| `title` | Human name shown by hosts. |
| `resource` | Name of a folder in `src/resources`. Makes this an MCP App tool with a View. Leave it out for a text-only tool. |
| `visibility` | `["model", "app"]` (default), `["model"]`, or `["app"]` for a helper only your View may call. See [Tool visibility](/docs/mcp-apps/visibility). |
| `annotations` | MCP hints: `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`. |
| `invoking`, `invoked` | Short status texts ChatGPT shows while the tool runs and after. |
| `_meta` | Extra `_meta` keys merged into the tool definition. |

## What a handler can return

| Return | Becomes |
|---|---|
| A plain object | `structuredContent`, plus a JSON text copy in `content` for the model |
| A string | One text content block |
| A full `CallToolResult` (`{ content, structuredContent, isError, _meta }`) | Passed through as is |
| `throw new Error("...")` | `isError: true` with your message as text |

See [Tool results](/docs/mcp-apps/tool-results) for how hosts use each part.

## A text-only tool

```ts
// src/tools/moon-facts.ts
export const tool = { title: "Moon facts", description: "Answer a quick moon question in text." };
export default async function () {
  return "The Moon is 384,400 km away on average.";
}
```

## Validation errors

Input is validated against `schema` before your handler runs. A bad call returns a tool error naming the field, which `moonpeak test` and the inspector both show.


---

# Views

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/views/

```tsx
// src/resources/moon/moon.tsx
import { useToolData, useTheme, useCallTool } from "moonpeak";

export const resource = {
  title: "Moon phase",
  description: "Moon phase for a date with a 7-day strip",
  prefersBorder: true,
};

export default function Moon() {
  const { output, isPending, isError } = useToolData<{ date?: string }, { phase: string }>();
  const theme = useTheme();
  if (isError) return <p className="error">Something went wrong.</p>;
  if (isPending) return <p>Reading the sky…</p>;
  return <h1 className={theme}>{output?.phase}</h1>;
}
```

The default export is the View. moonpeak connects it to the host, mounts it and wraps it in an error boundary; you never touch `postMessage`.

## Styles

A CSS file in the folder named `<name>.css`, `style.css` or `styles.css` is imported automatically. Each View is built into one HTML file with its CSS and JS inlined, so it works under strict host CSPs. Style both themes: hosts can switch between light and dark at any time.

## Resource config

`export const resource = {...}` sets per-View options:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title`, `description` | Shown by hosts and used as ChatGPT's widget description. |
| `prefersBorder` | Ask the host to draw a border around the View. |
| `csp.connectDomains` | Origins the View may `fetch` from. |
| `csp.resourceDomains` | Origins for images, fonts and scripts. |
| `csp.frameDomains`, `csp.baseUriDomains` | Origins for nested frames and `<base>`. |
| `permissions` | Ask for `camera`, `microphone`, `geolocation` or `clipboardWrite`. |
| `domain` | A dedicated origin for the View, when the host supports it. |

See [Security & CSP](/docs/mcp-apps/security).

## Rules of thumb

- Call every hook before the first early `return`.
- Use one [`useAppState`](/docs/hooks/use-app-state) per View for state that should survive reloads.
- Talk to your server with [`useCallTool`](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool), not `fetch`, unless you set `csp.connectDomains`.
- Keep the View useful in a 320 px wide frame; check it with the inspector's mobile device.

## Hot reload

In `moonpeak dev`, saving a View hot-swaps the component and keeps its state. Saving the `resource` config or a tool takes effect on the next call without a page reload.


---

# Runtime APIs

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis/

Hooks from `moonpeak` work in every MCP Apps host. Hooks from `moonpeak/chatgpt` and `moonpeak/claude` are safe to call anywhere and return empty values outside their host.

## Tool data

| Hook | Returns |
|---|---|
| [useToolData](/docs/hooks/use-tool-data) | `{ input, output, content, isPending, isError, isStreaming, isCancelled, tool, result }` |
| [useToolInput](/docs/hooks/use-tool-input) | the tool input |
| [useToolOutput](/docs/hooks/use-tool-output) | the structured output |
| [useToolResult](/docs/hooks/use-tool-result) | the raw `CallToolResult` |

## Host context

| Hook | Returns |
|---|---|
| [useTheme](/docs/hooks/use-theme) | `"light" \| "dark"` |
| [useDisplayMode](/docs/hooks/use-display-mode) | `"inline" \| "pip" \| "fullscreen"` |
| [useRequestDisplayMode](/docs/hooks/use-request-display-mode) | a function to request a mode, plus `available` |
| [useHostContext](/docs/hooks/use-host-context) | the whole host context |
| [useLocale](/docs/hooks/use-locale) · [useTimeZone](/docs/hooks/use-time-zone) | locale and IANA time zone |
| [usePlatform](/docs/hooks/use-platform) · [useDeviceCapabilities](/docs/hooks/use-device-capabilities) | `web/desktop/mobile`, touch and hover |
| [useSafeArea](/docs/hooks/use-safe-area) · [useContainerSize](/docs/hooks/use-container-size) · [useMaxHeight](/docs/hooks/use-max-height) | layout limits |

## Host

| Hook | Returns |
|---|---|
| [useHost](/docs/hooks/use-host) | `{ name, version }` of the host |
| [useHostCapabilities](/docs/hooks/use-host-capabilities) | what the host supports |
| [useConnection](/docs/hooks/use-connection) | `{ status, ready, error }` |
| [useApp](/docs/hooks/use-app) | the raw MCP Apps SDK `App` |

## Actions

| Hook | Does |
|---|---|
| [useCallTool](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool) | call a tool on your server through the host |
| [useSendMessage](/docs/hooks/use-send-message) | post a message as the user |
| [useUpdateModelContext](/docs/hooks/use-update-model-context) | tell the model something silently |
| [useOpenLink](/docs/hooks/use-open-link) · [useDownloadFile](/docs/hooks/use-download-file) · [useLog](/docs/hooks/use-log) | host actions |

## State

| Hook | Does |
|---|---|
| [useAppState](/docs/hooks/use-app-state) | one state object per View, persisted in ChatGPT, optionally shared with the model |
| [useResultState](/docs/hooks/use-result-state) | local state that resets on every new result |

## Host extras

| Hook | From |
|---|---|
| [useIsChatGPT](/docs/hooks/use-is-chat-gpt), [useWidgetState](/docs/hooks/use-widget-state), [useOpenAiGlobal](/docs/hooks/use-open-ai-global), [useUploadFile](/docs/hooks/use-upload-file), [useRequestModal](/docs/hooks/use-request-modal), [useUserAgent](/docs/hooks/use-user-agent) | `moonpeak/chatgpt` |
| [useIsClaude](/docs/hooks/use-is-claude), [useClaudeStyles](/docs/hooks/use-claude-styles) | `moonpeak/claude` |

## Helpers

```ts
import { isHost, connect } from "moonpeak";
isHost(useHost(), "claude");   // forgiving host-name check
```

`connect()` is called for you when a View mounts. Call it yourself only if you render without moonpeak's entry (for example in a test harness).


---

# ChatGPT Apps

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/chatgpt/

ChatGPT Apps are MCP Apps. Every moonpeak resource carries both the MCP Apps metadata and the older ChatGPT Apps SDK keys, so ChatGPT renders your Views without extra work:

| moonpeak | ChatGPT key |
|---|---|
| tool `resource` | `openai/outputTemplate` |
| tool `invoking`, `invoked` | `openai/toolInvocation/invoking`, `.../invoked` |
| tool `visibility: ["app"]` | `openai/visibility: "private"` and `openai/widgetAccessible: true` |
| resource `description` | `openai/widgetDescription` |
| resource `prefersBorder` | `openai/widgetPrefersBorder` |
| resource `csp` | `openai/widgetCSP` |

## ChatGPT-only hooks

```tsx
import { useIsChatGPT, useWidgetState, useOpenAiGlobal, useUploadFile, useRequestModal, useUserAgent } from "moonpeak/chatgpt";
```

They read `window.openai` and do nothing outside ChatGPT. Prefer the portable hooks when one exists: [`useAppState`](/docs/hooks/use-app-state) already saves to ChatGPT's widget state.

## Try it in ChatGPT

1. Deploy over HTTPS (see [Deployment](/docs/guides/deployment)).
2. In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps → enable **Developer mode** → **Create app**.
3. Enter `https://your-domain/mcp` and save.
4. In a new chat, ask for something your tool handles.

The inspector's ChatGPT host replicates `window.openai` (globals, widget state, display modes), so most issues show up locally first.


---

# Claude connectors

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/claude/

Claude renders MCP Apps natively. Deploy your server and add it as a connector:

1. Deploy over HTTPS (see [Deployment](/docs/guides/deployment)).
2. In Claude: Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector**.
3. Enter `https://your-domain/mcp`.
4. Enable the connector in a chat and ask for something your tool handles.

## Claude-only hooks

```tsx
import { useIsClaude, useClaudeStyles } from "moonpeak/claude";

const vars = useClaudeStyles();   // fonts and colors Claude sends in host context
```

moonpeak already applies host style variables to the document, so `var(--font-sans)` and friends work in your CSS in every host that sends them.

## Auth

If your server needs a user's credentials, see [Authorization](/docs/guides/authorization).


---

# MCP server

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/mcp-server/

`moonpeak dev` and `moonpeak start` both build an MCP server from your project. You can also use the pieces yourself from `moonpeak/server`:

```ts
import { createMcpServer, createHandler, createNodeHandler, resourceUri, RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE } from "moonpeak/server";
```

| Export | What it does |
|---|---|
| `createMcpServer(opts)` | An `McpServer` (MCP TypeScript SDK v2) with every tool and `ui://` resource registered. |
| `createHandler(opts)` | A Fetch handler `(Request) => Promise<Response>` for Workers, Hono, Deno, Bun, Next.js. Stateless: one server per request. |
| `createNodeHandler(opts)` | A Node `(req, res)` handler for `http.createServer` and Express. |
| `resourceUri(app, name)` | `ui://<app>/<name>.html` |
| `RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE` | `text/html;profile=mcp-app` |

`opts` is `{ name, version?, instructions?, tools, resources }`. The easiest way to get it is from a build:

```ts
import { loadBuilt } from "moonpeak/server";   // reads dist/server.mjs + dist/resources (Node)
const opts = await loadBuilt(process.cwd());
```

or by importing `dist/server.mjs` and reading the HTML files yourself (see [Production server](/docs/app-framework/production-server)).

## Transport

Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, stateless. `POST` carries JSON-RPC; the optional `GET` stream answers `405` because the server never pushes. That is spec-compliant and every host handles it.


---

# Production server

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/app-framework/production-server/

```bash
moonpeak build     # dist/resources/<view>.html, dist/server.mjs, dist/manifest.json
moonpeak start     # serves /mcp and /health on $PORT or 8000
```

`dist/server.mjs` bundles your tools (dependencies stay external, so install them in production). Each `dist/resources/*.html` is one self-contained View.

## Endpoints

| Path | |
|---|---|
| `/mcp` | the MCP server (Streamable HTTP) |
| `/health` | `{ ok, name, version, tools }` for load balancers |

## Mount it yourself

```ts
// Express
import express from "express";
import { createNodeHandler, loadBuilt } from "moonpeak/server";

const app = express();
app.all("/mcp", await createNodeHandler(await loadBuilt(process.cwd())));
app.listen(8000);
```

```ts
// Cloudflare Workers, Hono, Deno, Bun
import { createHandler } from "moonpeak/server";
import * as built from "./dist/server.mjs";
// however your runtime imports text files (Wrangler text rules, Bun, Deno...)
import moon from "./dist/resources/moon.html";
import calendar from "./dist/resources/calendar.html";
const html = { moon, calendar };

const handle = createHandler({
  ...built.app,
  tools: built.tools,
  resources: built.resources.map((r) => ({ ...r, html: () => html[r.name] })),
});
export default { fetch: (req) => (new URL(req.url).pathname === "/mcp" ? handle(req) : new Response("ok")) };
```

Then put it behind HTTPS. See [Deployment](/docs/guides/deployment).


---

# useToolData

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-tool-data/

```ts
import { useToolData } from "moonpeak";

useToolData<In, Out>(): ToolData<In, Out>
```

Everything about the tool call this View was opened for: the input, your handler's structured output, the raw result and its state.

## Returns

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `In | undefined` | Tool arguments. While the model is still writing them, the partial input. |
| `output` | `Out | undefined` | The `structuredContent` your handler returned. |
| `content` | `ContentBlock[] | undefined` | The result's content blocks (text the model sees). |
| `isPending` | `boolean` | No result yet and not cancelled. Show a skeleton. |
| `isStreaming` | `boolean` | The host is still streaming the input. |
| `isError` | `boolean` | The tool returned `isError: true` (your handler threw). |
| `isCancelled` | `boolean` | The user or host cancelled the call. |
| `tool` | `{ name, title?, description? }` | Which tool this View belongs to. |
| `result` | `CallToolResult | undefined` | The whole result, including `_meta`. |

## Example

```tsx
import { useToolData } from "moonpeak";

export default function Moon() {
  const { output, isPending, isError, content } = useToolData<{ date?: string }, { phase: string }>();
  if (isError) return <p>{content?.[0]?.text}</p>;
  if (isPending) return <p>Reading the sky…</p>;
  return <h1>{output?.phase}</h1>;
}
```

## Notes

- Handle `isError` and `isPending` before reading `output`.
- Call every hook before the first early `return`.

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

---

# useToolInput

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-tool-input/

```ts
import { useToolInput } from "moonpeak";

useToolInput<In>(): In | undefined
```

Just the tool input (or the partial input while it streams).

## Example

```tsx
const input = useToolInput<{ date?: string }>();
```

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

# useToolOutput

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-tool-output/

```ts
import { useToolOutput } from "moonpeak";

useToolOutput<Out>(): Out | undefined
```

Just the structured content your handler returned.

## Example

```tsx
const output = useToolOutput<{ phase: string }>();
```

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

# useToolResult

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-tool-result/

```ts
import { useToolResult } from "moonpeak";

useToolResult<Out>(): CallToolResult<Out> | undefined
```

The raw `CallToolResult`: `content`, `structuredContent`, `isError` and `_meta`.

## Example

```tsx
const result = useToolResult();
const meta = result?._meta;
```

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

---

# useTheme

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-theme/

```ts
import { useTheme } from "moonpeak";

useTheme(): "light" | "dark"
```

The host's theme. Defaults to `"light"` before the host reports one. moonpeak also applies the host's CSS variables to the document.

## Example

```tsx
const theme = useTheme();
return <div className={`card ${theme}`}>…</div>;
```

## Notes

- Style both themes: hosts switch at any time without reloading the View.

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

# useDisplayMode

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-display-mode/

```ts
import { useDisplayMode } from "moonpeak";

useDisplayMode(): "inline" | "pip" | "fullscreen"
```

How the host is showing the View right now.

## Example

```tsx
const mode = useDisplayMode();
return <div className={`app mode-${mode}`}>…</div>;
```

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

---

# useRequestDisplayMode

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-request-display-mode/

```ts
import { useRequestDisplayMode } from "moonpeak";

useRequestDisplayMode(): ((mode) => Promise<DisplayMode>) & { available: DisplayMode[] }
```

Ask the host to switch display mode. Resolves to the mode the host actually granted; `available` lists what this host allows.

## Example

```tsx
const requestMode = useRequestDisplayMode();

{requestMode.available.includes("fullscreen") && (
  <button onClick={() => requestMode("fullscreen")}>Expand</button>
)}
```

## Notes

- Hosts may refuse a mode. Render from `useDisplayMode()`, not from what you asked for.

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

---

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

# useCallTool

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-call-tool/

```ts
import { useCallTool } from "moonpeak";

useCallTool(): (name: string, args?: object) => Promise<CallToolResult>
```

Call a tool on your MCP server through the host. Throws an `Error` with the tool's text when the result has `isError: true` (the result is on `err.result`).

## Example

```tsx
const callTool = useCallTool();

async function nextWeek() {
  const res = await callTool("show-moon", { date: "2026-12-01" });
  setState({ view: res.structuredContent, selected: 0 });
}
```

## Notes

- Tools marked `visibility: ["app"]` can be called here even though the model never sees them.

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

---

# useUpdateModelContext

```ts
import { useUpdateModelContext } from "moonpeak";
```

# useAppState

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-app-state/

```ts
import { useAppState } from "moonpeak";

useAppState<S>(initial: S, options?: { share?: boolean }): [S, (next: S | (prev: S) => S) => S]
```

State that belongs to this View instance. In ChatGPT it is saved with the message (widget state), so it survives reloads. With `{ share: true }` the model also sees it on its next turn (debounced 400 ms).

## Example

```tsx
const [state, setState] = useAppState({ selected: 0, more: [] }, { share: true });
setState((s) => ({ ...s, selected: 2 }));
```

## Notes

- It holds ONE object per View. Use it once, put every field in that object and pass pieces down. moonpeak warns in the console if it is used twice.

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

---

# useResultState

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/hooks/use-result-state/

```ts
import { useResultState } from "moonpeak";

useResultState<S>(initial: S | (result) => S): [S, (next: S) => void]
```

Like `useState`, but resets whenever a new tool result arrives. Good for UI state tied to one result, like an open row.

## Example

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useResultState<number | null>(null);
```

## Works in

Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector.

See all hooks in [Runtime APIs](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis).

# moon

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/resources/moon/

```bash
npx moonpeak new my-app moon
```

| Part | File |
|---|---|
| View | `src/resources/moon/moon.tsx`, `moon.css` |
| Tools | `src/tools/show-moon.ts` (with View), `src/tools/moon-facts.ts` (text only) |
| Tests | `tests/simulations/show-moon.json`, `moon-facts.json`, `tests/e2e/moon.spec.ts`, `tests/evals/moon.eval.json` |

## What it shows

- Reading tool data with [`useToolData`](/docs/hooks/use-tool-data) and handling pending and error states.
- Calling the same tool again from the View ("Week →") with [`useCallTool`](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool), keeping the new result in [`useAppState`](/docs/hooks/use-app-state).
- Posting a follow-up question with [`useSendMessage`](/docs/hooks/use-send-message).
- Asking for fullscreen with [`useRequestDisplayMode`](/docs/hooks/use-request-display-mode) and styling per display mode.
- A text-only sibling tool (`moon-facts`), so evals can check the model picks the right one.

The moon math in `src/lib/moon.ts` is real (synodic month from a known new moon), so no API is needed.


---

# calendar

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/resources/calendar/

```bash
npx moonpeak new my-app calendar
```

| Part | File |
|---|---|
| View | `src/resources/calendar/calendar.tsx`, `calendar.css` |
| Tool | `src/tools/moon-calendar.ts` (`from?`, `count` 1-12) |
| Tests | `tests/simulations/moon-calendar.json`, `tests/e2e/calendar.spec.ts`, `tests/evals/calendar.eval.json` |

## What it shows

- A horizontal scroll-snap carousel with previous and next buttons that works with touch, mouse and keyboard.
- **Pagination through the host**: "Load 4 more" calls `moon-calendar` again from the View and appends the result.
- **Shared state**: the selected card and loaded pages live in `useAppState(..., { share: true })`, so the model knows which phase the user picked.
- A schema limit (`count` max 12) with a simulation proving out-of-range input is a tool error.


---

# review

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/resources/review/

```bash
npx moonpeak new my-app review
```

| Part | File |
|---|---|
| View | `src/resources/review/review.tsx`, `review.css` |
| Tools | `src/tools/plan-night.ts` (model-visible, with View), `src/tools/confirm-plan.ts` (app-only) |
| Tests | `tests/simulations/plan-night.json`, `confirm-plan.json`, `tests/e2e/review.spec.ts`, `tests/evals/review.eval.json` |

## The pattern

1. The model calls `plan-night` with a date and place. It returns a **proposal** (`status: "proposed"`) with sky darkness and targets, and suggests a darker night when the moon is bright.
2. The View shows the proposal with **Confirm plan** and **Pick another night**.
3. **Confirm** calls `confirm-plan` with [`useCallTool`](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool). That tool has `visibility: ["app"]`, so hosts never offer it to the model: only the user's click can confirm. The View then tells the model with [`useUpdateModelContext`](/docs/hooks/use-update-model-context).
4. **Decline** posts a follow-up with [`useSendMessage`](/docs/hooks/use-send-message), asking for the darker night.

The decision is kept in `useAppState`, so a confirmed plan stays confirmed after a reload. Use the same shape for anything the model should propose but the user must approve: bookings, payments, sending email.


---

# moonpeak new

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/new/

```bash
npx moonpeak new [name] [resources] [--install | --no-install] [-y]
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `name` | Folder and package name. Asked for when missing (default `moonpeak-app`). |
| `resources` | Comma-separated: `moon`, `calendar`, `review`, or `all`. Asked for when missing. |
| `--install` / `--no-install` | Install dependencies, or don't, without asking. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Accept every default. |

Outside a terminal (CI, scripts) `new` never prompts: it uses the defaults and does not install.

```bash
npx moonpeak new moon-app calendar,review --install
pnpm dlx moonpeak new moon-app          # uses pnpm for the install and next steps
```

The target folder must be empty or missing.


---

# moonpeak dev

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/dev/

```bash
moonpeak dev [--port 3000] [--open]
```

Starts one HTTP server with:

| Path | |
|---|---|
| `/` | the inspector |
| `/mcp` | your MCP server (Streamable HTTP) |
| `/__moonpeak/view/<name>` | a View with Vite HMR |

Saving a View hot-swaps it and keeps its state; saving a tool takes effect on the next call. If the port is busy, the next free one is used. The server only answers on `localhost` (requests with another `Host` header get `403`), which blocks DNS-rebinding attacks from web pages.

`--open` opens the inspector in your browser. The port can also come from `moonpeak.config.js`.


---

# moonpeak build

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/build/

```bash
moonpeak build [--out dist]
```

Writes (into `--out`, default `dist`):

| File | |
|---|---|
| `dist/resources/<name>.html` | each View with its JS and CSS inlined |
| `dist/server.mjs` | your tools and resource configs, bundled (dependencies external) |
| `dist/manifest.json` | app name, version, tools and resources |

Serve it with [`moonpeak start`](/docs/cli/start) or mount it yourself ([Production server](/docs/app-framework/production-server)).


---

# moonpeak start

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/start/

```bash
moonpeak start [--port 8000] [--out dist]
```

Serves the build in `--out` (default `dist/`) on `0.0.0.0`: `/mcp` and `/health`. The port is `--port`, else `$PORT`, else `8000`. Run `moonpeak build` first.


---

# moonpeak inspect

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/inspect/

```bash
moonpeak inspect --server <url> [--header k:v]... [--port 3000]
```

```bash
moonpeak inspect --server http://localhost:8000/mcp
moonpeak inspect --server https://api.example.com/mcp --header "authorization:Bearer $TOKEN"
moonpeak inspect --server https://moonpeak-ai.com/mcp
```

The inspector proxies `/mcp` to the server (adding your headers), lists its tools, reads `ui://` resources with `resources/read` and renders them exactly like a host. Simulations come from `tests/simulations/` in the current folder, so you can keep fixtures for a server that moonpeak didn't build (`moonpeak test init --server` writes them). See [Remote servers](/docs/inspector/remote).


---

# moonpeak test

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/test/

```bash
moonpeak test [--filter text]          # schemas, Views, simulations (in-process)
moonpeak test --e2e                    # Playwright against the inspector
moonpeak test --visual [--update]      # @visual screenshot tests
moonpeak test --eval                   # model evals
moonpeak test --server <url> [--header k:v]   # all of the above against another server
moonpeak test init [--server <url>]    # write a simulation per tool
```

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--filter <text>` | only tools or simulations whose name contains the text |
| `--e2e` | runs your Playwright config; excludes `@visual` tests |
| `--visual` | runs only `@visual` tests; records missing baselines |
| `--update` | with `--visual`: re-record every baseline |
| `--eval` | runs `tests/evals/*.eval.json`; needs provider keys |
| `--server <url>` | test a remote server instead of this project |
| `--header k:v` | extra request header, repeatable |

In a folder without `src/tools` that has a `moonpeak.test.json` (`{ "server": "https://..." }`, written by `test init --server`), `moonpeak test` tests that server automatically.

Exit code is `0` when everything passed, `1` otherwise, so it drops into CI. See [Testing Framework](/docs/testing).


---

# moonpeak upgrade

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/cli/upgrade/

```bash
moonpeak upgrade
```

Installs `moonpeak@latest` with the package manager that ran the command. `moonpeak --version` prints the installed version.


---

# Testing Framework

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/

moonpeak tests at five levels. Start with the first and add the others when you need them.

| Level | Command | Needs | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| [In-process checks](/docs/testing/unit) | `moonpeak test` | nothing | seconds |
| [E2E](/docs/testing/e2e) | `moonpeak test --e2e` | Chromium (Playwright) | seconds |
| [Visual regression](/docs/testing/visual) | `moonpeak test --visual` | Chromium | seconds |
| [Evals](/docs/testing/evals) | `moonpeak test --eval` | provider API keys | depends on the model |
| [Any MCP server](/docs/testing/any-server) | `--server <url>` | a running server | same as above |

All of them read the same [simulations](/docs/testing/simulations): JSON fixtures that also drive the inspector, so the scenario you look at is the scenario you test.

```text
  moonpeak test my-app

  ✓ schema     plan-night
  ✓ view       ui://my-app/review.html
  ✓ sim        plan-night#dark-new-moon-night
  ✗ sim        plan-night#bad-date
      expected isError true, got false

  1 failed · 21 checks · 7.1s
```

Ready-made CI setup: [CI](/docs/testing/ci).


---

# Simulations

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/simulations/

One file per tool in `tests/simulations/<tool>.json`, holding one simulation or an array:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "full moon",
    "prompt": "What does the moon look like on Nov 24, 2026?",
    "input": { "date": "2026-11-24" },
    "expect": { "output": { "phase": "Full Moon", "week": { "$length": 7 } } }
  },
  {
    "name": "mocked crescent",
    "input": {},
    "output": { "phase": "Waxing Crescent", "illumination": 0.11 },
    "host": { "name": "claude", "theme": "dark", "device": "mobile" }
  },
  {
    "name": "bad date",
    "input": { "date": "soon" },
    "expect": { "isError": true, "text": "not a date" }
  }
]
```

## Fields

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `name` | Shown in the inspector and test output. In a file with several simulations the id is `<tool>#<slug of name>` (e.g. `show-moon#full-moon`); a file with one simulation uses the tool name as its id. |
| `tool` | Which tool; defaults to the file name. |
| `prompt` | What a user might ask. Shown in the inspector's chat. |
| `input` | Tool arguments. |
| `output` / `result` | **Mock** the tool result (`output` = structuredContent, `result` = a whole CallToolResult). The handler is not called, so you can design a View before the backend exists. |
| `expect` | What `moonpeak test` checks (below). |
| `host` | Inspector settings for this scenario: `name` (`chatgpt` or `claude`), `theme`, `displayMode` (`inline`, `pip`, `fullscreen`), `device` (`desktop`, `tablet`, `mobile`), `locale`. |

## Expectations

| Key | Passes when |
|---|---|
| `isError` | the result's `isError` matches |
| `text` | the result's text contains the string (or every string in an array) |
| `output` | **partial match** against `structuredContent` |

Inside `output`:

| Matcher | Example | Matches |
|---|---|---|
| literal | `"phase": "Full Moon"` | equal value |
| object | `{ "week": {...} }` | listed keys only, extra keys ignored |
| array | `[{ "phase": "Full Moon" }]` | element by element, partial |
| `"re:..."` | `"re:^MP-[0-9A-Z]{6}$"` | regular expression |
| `"*"` | `"ref": "*"` | any value, as long as the key exists |
| `$length` | `{ "$length": 7 }` | array length |
| `$minLength` | `{ "$minLength": 1 }` | at least that many |

## Writing them for an existing server

```bash
moonpeak test init --server http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

writes a starter simulation per tool (with example input built from its schema) plus `moonpeak.test.json`. Running it again only adds files for new tools.


---

# In-process checks

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/unit/

```bash
moonpeak test [--filter plan-night]
```

Runs your real handlers in-process over an in-memory MCP transport:

1. **Setup**: the project has tools. An empty project fails loudly instead of passing.
2. **Schema**: every tool lists with a valid input schema (and output schema if you set one).
3. **View**: every `ui://` resource builds and returns HTML with the MCP Apps MIME type.
4. **Simulations**: every simulation with `expect` runs against the handler (or its mocked output) and is checked.

Nothing leaves your machine. Use `--filter` to run one tool or simulation.


---

# E2E testing

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/e2e/

```bash
npx playwright install chromium   # once
moonpeak test --e2e
```

moonpeak starts the inspector for your project and runs your Playwright config. Tests import from `moonpeak/test`:

```ts
import { test, expect } from "moonpeak/test";

test("renders in Claude dark mode", async ({ inspector }) => {
  const view = await inspector.open({ tool: "show-moon", sim: "show-moon#full-moon", host: "claude", theme: "dark" });
  await expect(view.getByRole("heading", { name: "Full Moon" })).toBeVisible();
});

test("asking posts a message", async ({ inspector }) => {
  const view = await inspector.open({ tool: "show-moon", sim: "show-moon#full-moon" });
  await view.getByRole("button", { name: "Ask about this night" }).click();
  await expect(inspector.sentMessages()).toContainText("full moon");
});

test("tool output", async ({ mcp }) => {
  expect(await mcp.call("show-moon", { date: "2026-11-24" })).toHaveStructuredContent({ phase: "Full Moon" });
});
```

## `inspector` fixture

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `open({ tool, sim, host, theme, device, mode })` | opens the inspector with those settings and returns a frame locator for the View once it has rendered |
| `view()` | the current View's frame locator |
| `sentMessages()` | locator for messages the View posted |
| `modelContext()` | locator for what the View told the model |
| `setTheme(t)`, `setDisplayMode(m)` | change host settings without reloading the View |
| `page` | the Playwright page |

## `mcp` fixture

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `call(name, args)` | call a tool, returns the `CallToolResult` |
| `listTools()` | the server's tools, with `_meta` |
| `client` | the raw MCP client |

## Matchers

`toHaveStructuredContent(partial)`, `toBeError()` and `toHaveTextContent(text)`, using the same partial matching as simulations.


---

# Visual regression

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/visual/

```ts
test("@visual crescent in both hosts", async ({ inspector }) => {
  for (const host of ["chatgpt", "claude"] as const) {
    const view = await inspector.open({ tool: "show-moon", sim: "show-moon#mocked-crescent", host });
    await expect(view.locator(".moon-app")).toHaveScreenshot(`crescent-${host}.png`, { maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01 });
  }
});
```

```bash
moonpeak test --visual            # runs @visual tests; records missing baselines
moonpeak test --visual --update   # re-record after an intended change
```

`--e2e` skips `@visual` tests, so functional runs stay fast. Use a **mocked** simulation for screenshots so data never changes between runs.

Baselines are platform specific (fonts render differently on Windows, macOS and Linux). Record them on the platform that checks them, usually CI, and keep `__screenshots__` out of git otherwise.


---

# Evals

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/evals/

```json
// tests/evals/moon.eval.json
{
  "models": ["claude-opus-5-5", "gpt-5"],
  "runs": 3,
  "passRate": 1,
  "system": "You are a helpful astronomy assistant.",
  "cases": [
    { "prompt": "what does the moon look like on 2026-11-24?", "expect": { "tool": "show-moon", "args": { "date": "2026-11-24" } } },
    { "prompt": "quick: moon phase on 2026-12-09, just text", "expect": { "tool": "moon-facts" } },
    { "prompt": "write me a haiku about autumn", "expect": { "tool": null } }
  ]
}
```

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... moonpeak test --eval
```

For every case and model, moonpeak sends your tool list (names, descriptions, input schemas) and the prompt, `runs` times, and checks which tool the model called:

| `expect` | Passes when |
|---|---|
| `"tool": "name"` | the model called that tool |
| `"tool": null` | the model called no tool |
| `"args": {...}` | the arguments partially match |

A case passes when at least `passRate` of its runs pass (default: all of them). Tools with `visibility: ["app"]` are never sent, because hosts never show them to the model.

## Providers

| Model names | Needs |
|---|---|
| `claude-*` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` in your project |
| `gpt-*`, `o1`/`o3`/`o4-*`, `chatgpt-*` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `openai` in your project |

`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL` are respected, so evals can run against a proxy or a gateway. Evals are the one mode that costs money; keep `runs` small and run them on demand rather than on every push.


---

# Any MCP server

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/any-server/

Everything in the testing framework works against a server moonpeak didn't build, over Streamable HTTP:

```bash
# write fixtures for each tool, plus moonpeak.test.json
moonpeak test init --server http://localhost:8000/mcp

# edit tests/simulations/*.json, then
moonpeak test                       # picks the server up from moonpeak.test.json
moonpeak test --server http://localhost:8000/mcp --header "authorization:Bearer $TOKEN"

# look at its Views
moonpeak inspect --server http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

The folder only needs `tests/simulations/` (and optionally `tests/e2e/`, `tests/evals/`). No `src/`, no build.

If the server can't be reached, moonpeak says so with the URL instead of a stack trace, and exits `1`.


---

# CI

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/testing/ci/

```yaml
# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: test
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with: { node-version: 22, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx moonpeak test
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npx moonpeak test --e2e
```

For a server in another language, start it in the background first, then point `--server` at it.

Pin `ubuntu-24.04`: Playwright's `--with-deps` installs system packages and only supports the Ubuntu versions it knows. Run `--eval` in a separate, manually triggered workflow with your provider keys as secrets.


---

# Inspector

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/inspector/

```bash
moonpeak dev                                         # your project
moonpeak inspect --server https://moonpeak-ai.com/mcp  # any server
```

The inspector is a real MCP Apps host: it connects to your server with the MCP client, reads `ui://` resources and renders them in a sandboxed iframe through the official `AppBridge`, exactly like ChatGPT and Claude do.

## Sidebar

| Control | |
|---|---|
| Tool | every tool on the server; tools with a View first |
| Simulation | fixtures for that tool; picking one runs it |
| Host | ChatGPT-style or Claude-style chrome, host info and capabilities |
| Theme | light or dark, sent live to the View |
| Device | desktop, tablet or mobile width (mobile also reports a touch platform) |
| Display mode | inline, picture-in-picture or fullscreen |
| Input | edit the arguments and **Run** the real handler |
| Output | edit the structured content and **Apply** to re-render without a backend |
| Log | every bridge message and `useLog` call |

## What the View can do

Calls to `callTool`, `sendMessage`, `updateModelContext`, `openLink`, `downloadFile` and display mode requests are handled like a host would: tools run against your server, messages appear in the chat, model context appears in a panel, links open in a new tab and downloads save. In the ChatGPT host, `window.openai` is there too (globals, widget state).

Everything you set lives in the URL. See [URL parameters](/docs/inspector/url-parameters).


---

# URL parameters

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/inspector/url-parameters/

```text
http://localhost:3000/?tool=show-moon&sim=show-moon%23full-moon&host=claude&theme=dark&device=mobile&mode=fullscreen
```

| Parameter | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `tool` | a tool name | first tool with a View |
| `sim` | a simulation id (`tool#name`, URL-encode the `#` as `%23`) | first simulation of the tool |
| `host` | `chatgpt`, `claude` | `chatgpt` |
| `theme` | `light`, `dark` | `light` |
| `device` | `desktop`, `tablet`, `mobile` | `desktop` |
| `mode` | `inline`, `pip`, `fullscreen` | `inline` |
| `locale` | BCP 47 tag | the browser's |
| `panel` | `input`, `output`, `log` | `input` |

E2E tests open the inspector through the same parameters (`inspector.open({...})`).


---

# Remote servers

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/inspector/remote/

```bash
moonpeak inspect --server https://api.example.com/mcp --header "authorization:Bearer $TOKEN"
```

- The inspector runs on localhost and proxies `/mcp` to the server, adding the headers server-side, so tokens never reach the page.
- Views are loaded with `resources/read`, like a host does, and rendered in the same sandbox.
- Simulations come from `tests/simulations/` in the folder you ran the command in.
- Servers that don't offer the optional `GET` stream (they answer `405`) are handled quietly.

Try it on the live demo: `npx moonpeak inspect --server https://moonpeak-ai.com/mcp`.


---

# MCP Apps

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/

An **MCP App** is an MCP tool that comes with a UI. The protocol is the [MCP Apps extension](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) to the Model Context Protocol, supported by ChatGPT (where they are called ChatGPT Apps), Claude, VS Code, Goose and others.

## The pieces

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Tool** | A normal MCP tool whose definition carries `_meta.ui.resourceUri`. |
| **UI resource** | An HTML document at a `ui://` URI with MIME type `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. |
| **View** | That HTML running in a sandboxed iframe in the host. |
| **Bridge** | A small JSON-RPC protocol over `postMessage` between the View and the host. |

## What happens on a tool call

1. The model calls your tool. The host sees `_meta.ui.resourceUri` and reads the resource with `resources/read`.
2. The host renders the HTML in a sandboxed iframe and connects the bridge.
3. The host sends the View its **host context** (theme, display mode, locale, size...) and the **tool input**, then the **tool result** when your handler returns.
4. The View can call tools, post messages, update model context, open links or ask for another display mode. The host decides whether to allow each request.

In moonpeak, steps 1 to 3 are the framework's job. Your View reads the result with [`useToolData`](/docs/hooks/use-tool-data) and acts with the [action hooks](/docs/app-framework/runtime-apis#actions).

## Why it matters

The same server works in every host that supports MCP Apps. You don't build a ChatGPT version and a Claude version: you build one MCP App and test it in both host styles with the [inspector](/docs/inspector).


---

# Lifecycle

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/lifecycle/

| Stage | `useConnection().status` | `useToolData()` |
|---|---|---|
| Mounted, bridge connecting | `connecting` | `isPending: true` |
| Connected, model still writing arguments | `ready` | `isStreaming: true`, partial `input` |
| Arguments final, tool running | `ready` | `input` set, `isPending: true` |
| Result arrived | `ready` | `output`, `content`, `isPending: false` |
| Tool threw | `ready` | `isError: true`, message in `content` |
| User cancelled | `ready` | `isCancelled: true` |

A View may also be shown again later for an old message (for example after a page reload in ChatGPT). Keep anything the user changed in [`useAppState`](/docs/hooks/use-app-state) so it comes back.

When a View calls a tool itself with [`useCallTool`](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool), that result comes back as the promise's value. It does not replace the result the View was opened with; store it in state if you render from it.


---

# Display modes & layout

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/display-modes/

| Mode | Where | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `inline` | in the message list, as wide as the chat | cards, small tables, carousels |
| `pip` | a floating window that stays while the user scrolls | timers, players, live status |
| `fullscreen` | covers the chat | maps, editors, long lists |

Read the current mode with [`useDisplayMode`](/docs/hooks/use-display-mode) and request a change with [`useRequestDisplayMode`](/docs/hooks/use-request-display-mode). The host may refuse; `available` lists the modes it allows.

## Sizing

- **Height**: inline Views grow to their content; moonpeak reports size changes to the host automatically. Respect [`useMaxHeight`](/docs/hooks/use-max-height) and scroll inside the View beyond it.
- **Width**: assume anything from 320 px (phones) to about 760 px. Test with the inspector's `mobile` device.
- **Safe areas**: in fullscreen on phones, pad by [`useSafeArea`](/docs/hooks/use-safe-area).


---

# State persistence

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/state/

[`useAppState`](/docs/hooks/use-app-state) holds one object per View instance:

```tsx
const [state, setState] = useAppState({ selected: 0, more: [] }, { share: true });
```

| Where | What happens |
|---|---|
| ChatGPT | saved as the message's widget state, restored when the View is shown again |
| Other hosts | kept for as long as the View lives |
| `{ share: true }` | also sent to the model as context (debounced 400 ms), so "the one I picked" makes sense to it |

Use [`useResultState`](/docs/hooks/use-result-state) for throwaway UI state that should reset when a new result arrives.

Anything that must outlive the conversation (orders, saved plans) belongs on your server: call a tool to save it.


---

# Tool visibility

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/visibility/

```ts
export const tool = {
  title: "Confirm stargazing plan",
  description: "Confirm a proposed plan. Called from the review View only.",
  visibility: ["app"],
};
```

| `visibility` | Model can call | View can call |
|---|---|---|
| `["model", "app"]` (default) | yes | yes |
| `["model"]` | yes | no |
| `["app"]` | no | yes |

moonpeak writes `_meta.ui.visibility` on the tool, plus `openai/visibility: "private"` and `openai/widgetAccessible: true` for ChatGPT, whether or not the tool has a View of its own. Hosts leave app-only tools out of the model's tool list, and `moonpeak test --eval` does too.

Use app-only tools for anything that needs the user's explicit action: confirming, paying, deleting. The [review](/docs/resources/review) resource is a full example.

App-only tools are still reachable by anyone who can call your server directly, so check permissions in the handler as you would for any endpoint.


---

# Security & CSP

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/security/

Hosts render Views in a sandboxed iframe with a strict Content Security Policy. By default a View can run its own inlined JS and CSS (which is how `moonpeak build` ships it) and talk to the host over the bridge. It cannot fetch other origins, load remote scripts or open popups on its own.

## Allowing more

```tsx
export const resource = {
  title: "Map",
  csp: {
    connectDomains: ["https://api.example.com"],     // fetch / WebSocket
    resourceDomains: ["https://tiles.example.com"],  // images, fonts, scripts
  },
  permissions: { geolocation: {} },
};
```

moonpeak sends these as MCP Apps `_meta.ui.csp` / `permissions` and as ChatGPT's `openai/widgetCSP`. Ask only for what you use; hosts may review apps that ask for more.

## Good practice

- Prefer [`useCallTool`](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool) over `fetch`: the call goes through the host to your server, with no CSP entry and no secrets in the View.
- Never put API keys in a View. Everything in it is visible to the user.
- Treat tool input as untrusted: validate with `schema`, and check permissions in handlers, including app-only ones.
- Use [`useOpenLink`](/docs/hooks/use-open-link) for links so the host can show its own confirmation.


---

# Tool results

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/mcp-apps/tool-results/

A `CallToolResult` has three parts, read by different consumers:

| Part | Read by | Put here |
|---|---|---|
| `content` | the **model** | a short text summary the model can talk about |
| `structuredContent` | the **View** (and the model, in hosts that pass it) | the data the View renders |
| `_meta` | the **View** only | data the model should not see (ids, large payloads, signed URLs) |

When your handler returns a plain object, moonpeak puts it in `structuredContent` and a JSON copy in `content`. For large data, return the shape yourself so the model gets a summary:

```ts
export default async function ({ from }) {
  const events = upcomingPhases(parseDate(from), 8);
  return {
    content: [{ type: "text", text: `Next: ${events[0].phase} on ${events[0].date}.` }],
    structuredContent: { from, events },
  };
}
```

Throwing returns `isError: true` with your message as text. The View sees `isError` in [`useToolData`](/docs/hooks/use-tool-data); [`useCallTool`](/docs/hooks/use-call-tool) throws it as an `Error`.


---

# Deployment

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/guides/deployment/

Hosts need a public HTTPS URL. The simplest setup is a VPS with Node and a reverse proxy.

## Node on a server

```bash
npm ci
npm run build
PORT=8000 npm start          # /mcp and /health
```

Keep it running with systemd, pm2 or a container. A minimal systemd unit:

```ini
[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/opt/my-app
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node node_modules/moonpeak/bin/moonpeak.mjs start --port 8000
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
Restart=always
```

## HTTPS with nginx

```nginx
location = /mcp {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header Connection "";
    proxy_buffering off;          # responses are streamed (SSE)
    proxy_read_timeout 120s;
}
```

Get a certificate with `certbot --nginx -d your-domain`. Add `limit_req` on `/mcp` if the server is public.

## Serverless and edge

Mount `createHandler` from `moonpeak/server` (Fetch API) on Workers, Deno Deploy, Bun or a Next.js route; see [Production server](/docs/app-framework/production-server). The handler is stateless, so it scales horizontally without sticky sessions.

## After deploying

```bash
npx moonpeak test --server https://your-domain/mcp    # same checks, against production
```

Then add `https://your-domain/mcp` in Claude (Connectors) or ChatGPT (Developer mode → Create app). The moonpeak demo at `https://moonpeak-ai.com/mcp` is deployed exactly this way.


---

# Authorization

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/guides/authorization/

moonpeak's server has no built-in auth: put it behind the auth your platform already uses.

## Protecting your server

Mount the handler behind a middleware that checks the request before it reaches `/mcp`:

```ts
import express from "express";
import { createNodeHandler, loadBuilt } from "moonpeak/server";

const mcp = await createNodeHandler(await loadBuilt(process.cwd()));
const app = express();
app.all("/mcp", (req, res, next) => {
  if (req.headers.authorization !== `Bearer ${process.env.MCP_TOKEN}`) return res.status(401).end();
  next();
}, mcp);
app.listen(8000);
```

For per-user access in Claude and ChatGPT, implement OAuth 2.1 as described in the MCP authorization spec (protected resource metadata plus an authorization server); hosts run the user through the login flow when they add your connector. Handlers can then read the verified user from the request in your middleware.

## Testing protected servers

```bash
moonpeak test --server https://api.example.com/mcp --header "authorization:Bearer $TOKEN"
moonpeak inspect --server https://api.example.com/mcp --header "authorization:Bearer $TOKEN"
```

The inspector adds headers server-side in its proxy, so the token is never exposed to the page.


---

# Patterns

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/guides/patterns/

## Detail card

One result, rendered richly, with buttons that call the same tool again with new arguments. Example: [moon](/docs/resources/moon).

## Carousel

A horizontal list of cards for browsing. Load more pages with `useCallTool` and keep them in `useAppState` with `share: true`, so the model knows which card the user picked. Example: [calendar](/docs/resources/calendar).

## Review and confirm

The model proposes an action, the user approves it in the View, and an app-only tool performs it. The model cannot skip the click. Example: [review](/docs/resources/review).

## Text tool next to a UI tool

Offer a text-only tool for quick answers and a UI tool for exploring. Describe both clearly and add eval cases that check the model picks the right one.

## Summary for the model, data for the View

Return a short `content` summary and the full data in `structuredContent` (see [Tool results](/docs/mcp-apps/tool-results)), so long lists don't fill the model's context.

## Keep the chat moving

After an important action, either post a message ([`useSendMessage`](/docs/hooks/use-send-message)) when the model should respond, or update model context ([`useUpdateModelContext`](/docs/hooks/use-update-model-context)) when it only needs to know.


---

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://moonpeak-ai.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/

## The View stays on its loading state

- The handler threw before returning: check the inspector's Log tab and the dev server output.
- `useAppState` is used in more than one component: it holds one object per View, so the calls overwrite each other. Use it once and pass values down (moonpeak warns in the console).
- You read `output` before checking `isPending`.

## "the View is not connected to a host yet"

An action hook was called during the first render. Call actions from event handlers or effects, not while rendering.

## A tool doesn't appear in ChatGPT or Claude

- The server isn't reachable over HTTPS from the internet: run `npx moonpeak test --server https://your-domain/mcp` from another machine.
- The tool is `visibility: ["app"]`: by design, the model never sees it.
- The host cached the old tool list: remove and re-add the connector or app.

## The model picks the wrong tool

Rewrite the `description` to say when to use the tool (and when not to), then measure with [evals](/docs/testing/evals).

## `moonpeak test --e2e` can't find a browser

Run `npx playwright install chromium` once (in CI, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` on `ubuntu-24.04`).

## Visual tests fail on another machine

Baselines are platform specific. Record them where they are checked: `moonpeak test --visual --update` on that platform.

## 403 from the dev server

`moonpeak dev` only answers to `localhost`. Open it as `http://localhost:3000`, not by IP or another host name.

## Something else

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/ghiansalman30-crypto/moonpeak/issues) with the inspector URL (it contains every setting).
